# A template written as a Go string literal is mutated too.
#
# The variation is spliced into the literal's text and the whole literal is
# re-encoded, so the overlay replaces the .go file rather than a template
# file. Positions are reported in the .go file, at the action itself.

muxt test-template-mutations
cmp stdout want.txt

-- go.mod --
module server

go 1.24
-- template.go --
package server

import "html/template"

var templates = template.Must(template.New("greeting").Parse(`Hello, {{.Name}}!{{if .Loud}} !!!{{end}}`))

type Greeting struct {
	Name string
	Loud bool
}
-- render_test.go --
package server

import (
	"strings"
	"testing"
)

func TestGreeting(t *testing.T) {
	var buf strings.Builder
	if err := templates.Execute(&buf, Greeting{Name: "World"}); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if got, want := buf.String(), "Hello, World!"; got != want {
		t.Errorf("greeting = %q, want %q", got, want)
	}
}
-- want.txt --
baseline ok
KILL template.go:5:70 "greeting" action-empty
MISS template.go:5:80 "greeting" if-false
KILL template.go:5:80 "greeting" if-true
3 mutants, 2 killed, 1 missed
